messages.subject: lavaan WARNING
parts:
Dear all,

Could someone please help me to solve the problem of running SEM with endogenous categorical variables?

I am new to lavaan.
After I ran SEM, I got a warning like this:

In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
lavaan WARNING: the optimizer (NLMINB) claimed the model converged,
but not all elements of the gradient are (near) zero;
the optimizer may not have found a local solution
use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check.  

Here is the syntax, when I run my model. 

sem0 <- 'attitude =~ family + health + independence

attitude ~ age + gender + education + background + order + encouragement + netincome + size + activity + marketing + pest + weather + offfarmincome + networking + government

objective ~ attitude + age + gender + education + background + order + encouragement + netincome + size + activity + marketing + pest + weather + offfarmincome + networking + government

happiness ~ attitude + objective + age + gender + education + background + order + encouragement + netincome + size + activity + marketing + pest + weather + offfarmincome + networking + government

probability ~ attitude + objective + happiness + age + gender + education + background + order + encouragement + netincome + size + activity + marketing + pest + weather + offfarmincome + networking + government'

fit0 <- sem(sem0, data=yfdata0, ordered=c("family","health","independence","objective","happiness","happiness"))    

My sample is only 176 people.

Thank you in advance,
Para

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan WARNING
parts: Could someone please help me to solve the problem of running SEM with endogenous categorical variables?

... I got a warning

Then the model ran.  Warnings indicate there might be a problem, not that there is one.  Although I wouldn't be surprised if your model were empirically underidentified, given your are almost certainly estimating as many parameters as there are people.  If your data were continuous, your syntax implies estimating 174 parameters:

lav_partable_npar(lavaanify(sem0))

Some of your outcomes are ordinal, and depending on the number of categories, you might be estimating even more parameters.  It will tell you near the top of the summary() output how many.  You could consider modeling one outcome at a time so that N > nParams in each model, but the N / nParams ratio would still be quite small, so warnings like this would not be a surprise.  I would recommend the regsem package, but it does not accommodate ordinal outcomes.

FYI:

You listed "happiness" twice.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
